decisions.title: How should personal-jacky project notes be seeded?
decisions.context: Claude Desktop MCP works; portfolio notes (ViOS, melody-thesis, …) are still thin. Autopilot should not invent personal content.

options.label: Founder + Claude Desktop seed manually (recommended)
options.implication: E-05 stays proposed; no Maker tasks until you ask.

options.label: Approve a Maker task that only creates stub notes with titles + links from project-registry.md
options.implication: Low-risk stubs; you fill bodies later.

decisions.recommendation: A — content quality matters more than stubs for a personal knowledge hub.
decisions.decided_note: Founder 2026-08-07: seed via Claude Desktop / manual; Autopilot must not invent personal note bodies.

decisions.title: Which credentials does the hub get, and scoped how?
decisions.context: E-09 collectors need two credentials the founder must create by hand. (1) A GitHub token that can READ jackyckma/{orbita,ai-transformation-io,powerhouse,ai-business,ViOS} — three are private, and an unauthenticated read returns 404, which a naive collector would record as 'no activity' rather than 'no access'. (2) A Zeabur API key for https://api.zeabur.com/graphql, created at Dashboard > Settings > API Keys; per Zeabur docs the key is tied to a personal account and carries that account's permissions across any team, so it cannot be narrowed to one project. NO BUILD REQUIRED: the credential vault already exists and runs in production — packages/lane-credentials, mounted at POST /v1/admin/credentials, write-once (409 on duplicate client_id+name), AES-encrypted with ORBITA_SECRETS_KEY, and the secret is never returned by any read route. Agents resolve secrets server-side via resolveCredentialSecret(clientId, name), already wired into the agent turn runner. Until the two rows exist, T-0051 and T-0052 can be built and unit-tested against fixtures but cannot be verified against real data.

options.label: Fine-grained GitHub PAT (contents: read-only, those 5 repos) + Zeabur API key (recommended)
options.implication: Least privilege available on both platforms. The Zeabur key is still account-wide — a platform limit, not a choice — so treat it as sensitive and rotate if the hub is ever exposed.

options.label: GitHub token only; defer Zeabur
options.implication: Line 1 works for all five projects; the merged-but-never-deployed blind spot stays open. T-0052 blocks.

options.label: Use a GitHub App instead of a PAT
options.implication: Better rotation and per-repo scoping, but meaningfully more setup for a single-operator portfolio.

decisions.recommendation: A — B leaves open the specific failure that is hardest to notice by eye (build fails, task still says done, prod smoke passes on the previous deployment). C is the right answer at larger scale, not at five repos with one operator.

_procedure._doc: CANONICAL credential names live here, not duplicated into task descriptions — T-0051/T-0052 unblock from this decision, so they inherit these. If a name changes, change it here only.
_procedure.write_once: Duplicate client_id+name returns 409. To replace a credential you must delete the row first — there is no update route. Get the value right before posting.

credentials.name: github_read
credentials.source: GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained. Repository access: only jackyckma/{orbita,ai-transformation-io,powerhouse,ai-business,ViOS}. Permission: Contents = Read-only. Nothing else.

_procedure.verify: GET https://api.get-orbita.com/v1/admin/credentials with the same admin header — returns metadata only (name, client_id, scopes, created_at). Secrets are never returned; seeing the two names listed is the confirmation.
